summary: Never reuse a writer's sequence after a trim deletes its newest batch

schema.detail: Adds the WITHOUT ROWID table writer_heads(writer, sequence, hash), one row per writer ever seen, and two triggers on batches (AFTER INSERT raises the head; BEFORE DELETE stores it). Rows are never deleted. Storage version stays 20; earlier binaries keep the triggers firing, which is harmless.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rule, admission or digest change. Local sequence allocation now also respects the stored head and the writer's own envelope tombstones, including those the retired-envelope ledger keeps after adoption withdraws them from checkpoint_envelopes, which changes the allocated sequence only when a trim had deleted the writer's newest batch: before this change that reused a sequence peers had already seen.

compatibility.detail: Wire format is unchanged. A returning member that previously would have reused a trimmed sequence now continues after it.

downtime.detail: Normal restart; the table and triggers are created empty at open. Each batch insert and batch delete adds one small upsert.

recovery.detail: Swapping back to an earlier binary is supported; the table and triggers remain. An earlier binary allocates from batches and the writer floor only.
